tasks.issue_text: Storage optimization crashes at the end of a deferred FTS rebuild on supported SQLite runtimes where the trigram tokenizer/index is unavailable. The base FTS index must still finish cleanly and remain searchable.

Deferred credential refresh correctly performs network work outside the pool lock, but the pool mutations that follow can race concurrent selection/rotation. Preserve the non-blocking refresh window while serializing the state mutation boundary.

CredentialPool.next_available_at() calls mutation-capable availability logic and iterates pool entries without the synchronization used by other pool readers. Make it safe against concurrent selection/rotation without changing reset-time semantics.

Dashboard session pagination and analytics window parameters are effectively unbounded, allowing one request to trigger excessive SQLite/profile fan-out or full-history analytics work. Add request-layer bounds while retaining normal in-range behavior.
The new profile fan-out request clamp rejects legitimate desktop callers that request 200 rows or over-fetch with an offset. Keep the endpoint bounded, but set the ceiling above real client maxima.

Async dashboard provider/custom-endpoint validation performs synchronous HTTP requests on the serving event loop. Preserve validation behavior and error classification while removing the blocking transport from async routes.

The dashboard plugins hub executes tool availability/auth probes inline and repeatedly rebuilds the same payload, making a read path perform potentially blocking auth/network/import work. Keep the request path read-only and cheap while preserving last-known auth hints.

After making the plugins hub read only, a dashboard-only session can keep an unknown tool-auth verdict forever because nothing warms a cold check_fn cache. Warm cold verdicts away from the request path and surface them on a later hub refresh.
